extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and professional writers, especially freelance and commercial fiction/nonfiction writers
extracted.subtask_description: A list of practical, career-focused pieces of advice for writers aiming to succeed commercially and professionally — covering work habits, submission strategy, editor relationships, and balancing paid versus personal projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing is Work
rubrics_metrics.description: It takes work. Lots and lots and lots of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat writing as labor that requires sustained effort; professionals keep producing regardless of inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for Your Audience, Not Yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional writing serves editors and readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor tone, content, and choices to what the market and audience expect rather than personal indulgence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach It as a Business
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial endeavor, not a romantic calling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage writing like a business: consider markets, pricing, contracts, deadlines, and profitability rather than relying on romantic notions of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Quit Your Day Job Early
rubrics_metrics.description: Only when freelance income exceeds salary by 30%+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be financially cautious; consider leaving steady employment only after freelance income reliably surpasses salary by a comfortable margin (Guideline: ~30%+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept Rejection as Inevitable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect rejection as part of the process, avoid taking it personally, and let it be motivating rather than discouraging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit Work Persistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmit rejected work to different markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistence in submissions increases chances of placement; don't treat a single rejection as final — target other appropriate markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Editor Guidelines Exactly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to submission guidelines (formatting, length, cover letters, etc.); failing to do so risks immediate rejection regardless of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to Editors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be collaborative and receptive to editorial feedback; resisting or arguing unnecessarily harms professional relationships and chances of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Flexible with Writing Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Success comes from willingness to write diverse content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness to different kinds of assignments and formats can create more opportunities than rigidly sticking to one form or genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build Contacts Through Professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Be nice; deliver quality; help others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional behavior, meeting deadlines, producing quality work, and being helpful to peers builds networks and future opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate Broad Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having a wide base of knowledge makes you more versatile and capable of writing on varied topics, enriching your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Paid and Personal Work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep doing personal or passion projects to maintain craft and enjoyment, even while pursuing paid assignments for income.
